paper_verdict.estimator_family: Panel fixed effects (robust SE), Hansen panel threshold regression, and 2SLS (internet penetration as instrument)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Exposure is an author-built composite DFI index (digital plus traditional financial inclusion, PCA, in percent), not a direct technology adoption measure; coefficients are semi-elasticities on log GDP per capita. Very short panel (3 years: 2014, 2017, 2021; N=90, 30 countries). Threshold regime coefficients are conditional on a single estimated threshold (71.87), not full-sample effects. The 2SLS coefficient (0.034) is about 7 times the FE estimate, with a possibly weak or questionable instrument (internet penetration). Estimates 45-1 and 45-4 are near duplicates (same specification, extra controls).

paper_verdict.estimator_family: Panel cointegration estimators: FMOLS and DOLS (long-run elasticities); also country-wise AMG
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome is log of GDP in current US dollars (aggregate level, not per capita or productivity); mobile subscriptions are in absolute numbers (not per capita) while internet users are in percent of population, so the elasticities are not comparable in units. Cointegration (FMOLS/DOLS) long-run elasticities with no reported n_obs (implied 10 x 17 = 170 but not printed); 10 emerging Asian countries chosen by highest GDP. Negative internet coefficient is likely a specification artifact (energy and income controls, GNI per capita IN also included). Reverse causality only examined via Dumitrescu-Hurlin Granger non-causality tests, not in the estimators.
